newsitem.title: USA: AMNEX unit buys pay phone assets in N.J.
newsitem.headline: AMNEX unit buys pay phone assets in N.J.

text.p: AMNEX Inc said on Tuesday its Crescent Public Communications Inc unit acquired substantially all of the assets of Coastal Telecom, Garden State and BEK Tel Inc, for about $4 million in cash and $8 million in unregistered stock.

The companies have combined assets of about 4,300 pay phones, it said. Under the agreement, AMNEX said it would acquire the telephone pay stations, along with related parts and supplies and the existing location contracts.

Coupled with the implementation of a recent U.S. Federal Communication Commission order prescribing "dial around" compensation for private pay phone owners, AMNEX said it expected its EBITDA from payphone operations alone to increase to about $7 million in 1997 on revenue of $18 million.
This compared with about $1 million in 1996 on revenues of about $7 million.
"Dial around" refers to customers using pay phones to dial numbers which do not require money, such as toll-free or emergency numbers, AMNEX said.
The FCC has come up with a system to compensate pay phone owners for such call, AMNEX said.
AMNEX said it would now own and operate about 6,500 pay phones in New York and New Jersey.
